identity.name: Lydia

union.text: the mainland Ionian and Aeolian coast that Croesus subjugates (ledger/10)

land.text: the whole Lydian kingdom, Sardis and everything west of the Halys that Croesus ruled, with the Ionian and Aeolian coast

successors.note: Lydia page: 'In 546 BC, it became a satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire, known as Sparda in Old Persian.' The Siege of Sardis page dates the fall to December 547 BC in its infobox and '547/546 BC' in its lead; Cliopatria's Achaemenid row starts in -550.

capitals.name: Sardis
capitals.note: Lydia infobox 'Capital: Sardis'. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Sardis (28.04 E, 38.49 N). The page gives no capital before Sardis.

rulers.name: Gyges
rulers.note: Lydia infobox '680-644 BC: Gyges'; the Gyges page's own infobox says c. 717-679 and its text and succession box c. 680-644.

rulers.name: Alyattes
rulers.note: Lydia infobox '635-585 BC'; the Lydia body text and the Alyattes page lead say c. 591-c. 560 and c. 618-c. 561; Alexander Dale's dating (c. 635-585) is the infobox's. Alyattes died 'shortly after the Battle of the Eclipse, in 585 BCE itself' (Alyattes page).

rulers.name: Croesus
rulers.note: Lydia infobox '585-546 BC'; the body text says c. 560-c. 546 and the Croesus page 'from 585 BC to 546 BC'.

keyframe_review.note: 24,042 km2 around Sardis (27.0-29.0 E), -700..-676. The Lydia page gives no infobox area and no extent for the early kings (it says only 'At its greatest extent, during the 7th century BC, it covered all of western Anatolia', which its own account of Alyattes and Croesus contradicts), so the core cannot be compared with an infobox figure. Gyges, 'the first Lydian king whose existence is demonstrable from contemporary records', reigns from c. 680 (Lydia infobox) or c. 717 (Gyges infobox). Cliopatria's Phrygia -700 shape (188,102 km2) covers this core as well; see the phrygia dossier.

24,824 km2, -675..-651: the same core with a small eastward growth (29.06 E). No page dates a Lydian gain in these years; the Gyges page says the Cimmerians 'destroyed Phrygia' c. 675 but gives the Troad to Gyges 'with little resistance after Phrygia's collapse' without a year (see the -650 event).

correction.text: Unchanged shape (Troad, Hellespont coast, Caria), held to 621 instead of 631; the Gyges page: the Gyges page has Lydia hold the Aegean coast of the Troad and the Hellespont coast including Abydos, and control Caria through alliances with the Carian dynasts at Mylasa and Pedasa

keyframe_review.note: 98,905 km2 (26.7-31.1 E, 36.9-41.2 N): Troad, Hellespont coast (Abydos) and Caria, which the Gyges page assigns to Gyges (680-644) without a year. The shape is drawn to -631; the Phrygia page puts the Lydian advance into Phrygia after the Cimmerians were expelled 'by around 620 BC', so the next shape should begin in -620. Years only.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held from 620 (to 616) instead of 630: 'Lydia then extended over much of Phrygia, which became the Lydian empire's eastern frontier.'

keyframe_review.note: 255,588 km2, reaching the Halys (35.2 E) and the Black Sea coast (42.0 N). The shape matches Alyattes's accession in Dale's dating (c. 635) but the pages date the eastward extension only as 'Lydia eventually expelled them [the Cimmerians] by around 620 BC. Lydia then extended over much of Phrygia' (Phrygia page); the Alyattes page gives it no year; the Halys border is fixed only by the Eclipse treaty of 585 and 'the actual border of his kingdom was further to the east of the Halys' (Lydia page). Years only: the shape holds from -620. No infobox area to compare.
255,809 km2, -615..-601: +0.2 percent over the previous shape; nothing on the pages explains the difference, which is below the precision of the era.

255,952 km2, -600..-551: the kingdom west of the Halys as Herodotus has Croesus rule it ('Croesus ruled over all the peoples to the west of the Halys River', Croesus page), which the Croesus page itself doubts: 'the eastern border would thus have instead been further to the east of the Halys'. The shape stops at 35.2 E, the Halys bend. Smyrna's capture (600) and the undated conquest of the Ionian mainland are inside the shape; no infobox area to compare.

union.text: the mainland Ionian and Aeolian coast that Croesus subjugates (ledger/10)

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held to 546 instead of 541.; plus the mainland Ionian and Aeolian coast (Ionia and Aeolis regions), which the dossier's ledger/10 gives to Lydia in -560 and which Cliopatria's Lydian shape leaves out (32 of the 83 cells of the two regions)

keyframe_review.note: 254,964 km2, -550..-541. The Lydian kingdom ends with the fall of Sardis: infobox 'Fall to Persia: 546 BC', 'In 546 BC, it became a satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire' (the Siege of Sardis page: December 547 BC). Years only: -550..-546; Cliopatria's Achaemenid row starts in -550, so the last five Lydian years overlap it in the data. [fx-43 R013] Croesus page: Croesus 'annexed Ephesus into the Lydian Empire' and 'subjugated all of mainland Ionia, Aeolis, and Doris'; Lydia holds the coast until the fall of Sardis in 546. Cliopatria's -550 shape holds only 51 of the 83 cells of Ionia and Aeolis, so the keyframe snap released 32 coastal cells to nobody and the Greek City-States' -550 keyframe took them back.

region.text: Lydia around Sardis, the Lydian kingdom core (Maeonia)

ledger.note: 700: the Lydian kingdom at Sardis under Gyges. Gyges is 'the first Lydian king whose existence is demonstrable from contemporary records' (Lydia page); the Gyges page infobox gives c. 717-679 BC for his reign while its text and the Lydia infobox give 680-644. The year is Cliopatria's first Lydia shape; Gyges overthrew King Candaules of the Heraclid dynasty, so a Lydian kingdom is older than the Mermnads.

region.text: the Aegean coast of the Troad and the Hellespont coast, including Abydos

ledger.note: 650: Gyges takes the Troad. The page (paraphrase): he took the region with little resistance after Phrygia's collapse, settled Lydians there and made Ilium an administrative centre. The page gives no year; -650 is Cliopatria's shape change inside Gyges's reign (680-644). The Phrygian collapse (c. 675) left the land to no state.

region.text: Caria, held through the Carian dynasts at Mylasa and Pedasa

ledger.note: 650: Caria under Lydian control. The Gyges page (paraphrase): through alliances with the Carian dynasts at Mylasa and Pedasa, Lydia controlled Caria; the Croesus page says Croesus brought Caria 'under the direct control of the Lydian Empire'. Neither dates it; -650 is Cliopatria's shape change.

region.text: much of Phrygia, the Lydian empire's eastern frontier

ledger.note: 620: Lydia takes Phrygia. 'Lydia eventually expelled them [the Cimmerians] by around 620 BC. Lydia then extended over much of Phrygia, which became the Lydian empire's eastern frontier.' The Alyattes page: 'Alyattes turned towards Phrygia in the east' (no year), with Lydian presence at Gordion; the Croesus page says Phrygian vassals owed military support and tribute. The land had no state since the Cimmerian sack of Gordion (phrygia dossier, -676).

region.text: the Mysians, Paphlagonians and Bithynians west of the Halys

ledger.note: 620: the northern peoples west of the Halys. The Croesus page: 'Croesus ruled over all the peoples to the west of the Halys River' including the Mysians, Paphlagonians and Bithynians, 'many [of whom] had already been conquered under Alyattes'; no year. -620 is the shape's extension, not a page's date.

612: the Lydian-Milesian War begins (infobox '612-600 BC'). The Alyattes page says the hostilities with Miletus 'lasted until Alyattes's sixth year (c. 630 BCE)' and then peace was made; the dates differ by two decades and the Lydia page's are used.
600: the war with Miletus ends (Lydia infobox '612-600 BC'). 'In 600 BCE, Alyattes resumed his military activities in the west' against Smyrna (Alyattes page).

region.text: Smyrna, the second Ionian city Alyattes attacked

ledger.note: 600: Alyattes takes Smyrna. 'In 600 BCE, Alyattes resumed his military activities in the west, and the second Ionian city he attacked was Smyrna'; he had new walls built there 'from around 600 to around 590 BCE'. Colophon: 'he placed Colophon itself under direct Lydian rule' (no year). Gyges had failed at Smyrna and taken only Colophon's lower city (Gyges page); Ardys 'succeeded in capturing the city of Priene' (Lydia page).

region.text: eastern Anatolia, the country either side of the Halys

ledger.note: 590: war with the Medes. 'a war broke out between the Median and Lydian Empires in 590 BC which was waged in eastern Anatolia', five years (Lydia page; the Alyattes page also says 590).

585: the Battle of the Eclipse ends the Median war. The battle was fought in the sixth year of the war; 'the eclipse of 28 May 585 BC' fits the place and era; the Halys 'was declared to be the border of the two warring kingdoms' and Alyattes's daughter Aryenis was married to Astyages, Cyaxares's son. The Lydia page: Nebuchadnezzar II and Syennesis of Cilicia mediated. The page gives no year for the treaty itself; the Alyattes page says the border was 'fixed at a yet undetermined location in eastern Anatolia' and the Halys line is a later Greek construction.

region.text: all of mainland Ionia, Aeolis, and Doris

ledger.note: 560 (page undated): Croesus subjugates the mainland Greek cities. 'Croesus annexed Ephesus into the Lydian Empire' and attacked other western-coast cities 'until he had subjugated all of mainland' Ionia, Aeolis and Doris; he made treaties of friendship with the islands. The year is the start of Croesus's reign by the Lydia body text (c. 560); the infobox says 585. Cliopatria already draws the Aegean coast from -650, so this event marks the page's claim, not a shape change.

547: Croesus crosses the Halys. 'In 547 BC, the Lydian king Croesus besieged and captured the Persian city of Pteria in Cappadocia'; the battle was a stalemate and the Lydians retreated to Sardis. The Siege of Sardis page has Cyrus then march on Sardis, defeat the Lydians at Thymbra and besiege the city for 14 days.

546: Sardis falls to Cyrus. 'Cyrus won and captured the capital city of Sardis by 546 BC.' The Siege of Sardis page (infobox) dates the siege to December 547 BC and its lead says 547/546; the Croesus page says there is no sure way of dating the fall.

union.text: the mainland Ionian and Aeolian coast that Croesus subjugates (ledger/10)

region.text: the Lydian kingdom to the Halys, with the Ionian and Aeolian coast

ledger.note: 546: the whole kingdom passes to Persia. 'In 546 BC, it became a satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire, known as Sparda in Old Persian'; the coastal Aeolian and Ionian cities, 'formerly Lydian tributaries, were likewise conquered not long afterward' (Siege of Sardis page). [fx-43 R013] Region widened with the Ionian and Aeolian coast of ledger/10, which Cliopatria's Lydian shape omits, so that the coast passes to Persia with the rest and is not left Lydian after the loss.

union.text: the mainland Ionian and Aeolian coast that Croesus subjugates (ledger/10)

region.text: the Lydian kingdom, from the Aegean coast to the Halys, with the Ionian and Aeolian coast

ledger.note: 546: Lydia ends. Infobox 'Fall to Persia: 546 BC'; 'Lydia would never regain its independence and would remain a part of various successive empires.' Date alternatives: December 547 (Siege of Sardis infobox), 547/546 (lead), 'traditionally fixed to 547 BC' and perhaps as late as 539 (Lydia and Croesus pages). [fx-43 R013] Region widened with the Ionian and Aeolian coast of ledger/10, which Cliopatria's Lydian shape omits, so that the coast passes to Persia with the rest and is not left Lydian after the loss.

wars.name: Cimmerian invasions of Lydia
wars.outcome: Gyges defeated the Cimmerians in 665 and survived a second invasion in 657; in 644, under Lygdamis, they defeated the Lydians, sacked Sardis and killed Gyges; in 637 they sacked Sardis again except its citadel. No land changed hands; Alyattes expelled them (Alyattes page: 'expelled' after a first victory early in his reign; Phrygia page: 'by around 620 BC').
wars.note: Dates from the Gyges page (665, 657, 644) and the Lydia page (644, 637); the Cimmerians had no state and no dossier.

wars.name: Lydian-Milesian War
wars.outcome: Peace with Miletus; Alyattes then turned on Smyrna (600).
wars.note: Lydia infobox '612-600 BC'; the Alyattes page says the hostilities ended in his sixth year (c. 630).

wars.name: Lydian-Median War
wars.outcome: Drawn by the eclipse of 28 May 585 BC; peace, the Halys as border, and Aryenis married to Astyages; Nebuchadnezzar II and Syennesis of Cilicia mediated.
wars.note: Lydia page: 'a war broke out ... in 590 BC ... lasted five years'.

wars.name: Persian conquest of Lydia
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Pteria (stalemate), Thymbra, a 14-day siege and the fall of Sardis; Lydia annexed by Persia, Croesus captured.

certainty.note: All Lydian frontiers are approximate: the Halys 'declared' as border in 585 is itself doubted (the real border lay further east), and no page gives a boundary for the coast or Caria.

notes:
Page budget: up to 5 pages; 6 Lydian pages were opened (Lydia, Gyges, Alyattes, Croesus, Battle of the Eclipse, Siege of Sardis) plus the Phrygia page, which belongs to the phrygia budget. No infobox area exists on any of them, so Cliopatria's areas (24k, 99k, 255k km2) are unchecked against a figure; the Lydia page's 'covered all of western Anatolia' in the 7th century is the only statement of extent and contradicts its own history.

Open points for a gap-filler: (1) the three eastern gains at -620 rest on one sentence of the Phrygia page and an undated Alyattes page; the Mysian, Bithynian and Paphlagonian conquests are not dated by any page opened. (2) The Ionian mainland: Cliopatria draws the Aegean coast (26.7 E) from -650, but the pages put Smyrna in 600 and Croesus's subjugation of the rest undated; the shape may be early for the coast. (3) Fall of Sardis: 546 (Lydia, Persian satrapy) against December 547 (Siege of Sardis infobox); end year -546 follows the state's own article; the Croesus page says no method can date the fall. (4) Alyattes's and Croesus's reign dates differ between the Lydia infobox (635-585, 585-546), the Lydia body text (c. 591-c. 560, c. 560-c. 546) and the Alyattes page (c. 618-c. 561 or Dale's c. 635-585). (5) Predecessors are left empty: the Lydia infobox lists Hittites, Phrygia, Cimmerians, Treri, Ionian League and the Achaemenid Empire without saying which is predecessor or successor. (6) Assyria: the Gyges page has Gyges send gifts but not tribute to Ashurbanipal c. 665 and support Psamtik I of Egypt c. 662-658; no land is involved, so there is no ledger event. Cliopatria's Lydia shape touches the Neo-Assyrian Empire and Assyrian Egypt in -630..-616, but no page opened says why.

Counterparts without a dossier: the Cimmerians (a people, not a state), the Carian dynasts of Mylasa and Pedasa. Region names the gazetteer lacks: Aeolis (Aeolian coast), Doris (Carian Doris/Dorian Hexapolis); both are used under 'Ionia/Aeolis' union with Aeolis flagged.
